summary: Single-author white-box case study of 'context rot' in a production-derived code-audit skill (4 audit tasks, 24 frozen mandatory checks), run mainly with Codex + gpt-5.4-mini. Clean 10,991-char context passes 8/10 runs; 299,140-char relevant and irrelevant contexts each pass 3/10 (Fisher p=0.0698), yet ~93% of individual checks still pass, so a few dropped obligations sink the artifact. A detailed external checklist restating all 24 obligations passes 10/10 vs 5/10 for a generic self-check (p=0.0325); a delegated sub-agent loses an opaque contract across native compaction in a single mechanism run.

claims.claim: Long context (299K chars) cuts strict pass from 8/10 to 3/10 on the main task
claims.evidence: §5.1.1/§5.2.1; two-sided Fisher p=0.0698, wide Wilson intervals; author explicitly calls it trend-level. One task, one model, n=10 per cell; sample sizes were extended after inspecting pilots (§7.2).

claims.claim: Requirement coverage stays >92% while strict success collapses: rot removes a few decisive obligations
claims.evidence: §5.3.1: long conditions satisfy 92.1-93.8% of checks; failures concentrated on the recurrent T002 array and cardinality rules.

claims.claim: No stable onset length; effect is task- and model-dependent
claims.evidence: §5.1.2-5.1.3, §5.2.2: 90K fails once then passes on replay; Revert SL-007 passes all clean and long runs; five-model probes sparse and uneven.

claims.claim: Detailed external checklist passes 10/10 vs 5/10 for generic self-check
claims.evidence: Table 7: 240/240 vs 234/240 checks; p=0.0325 two-sided; author notes single n=10 comparison may overestimate benefit; failure upper bound 27.8%.

claims.claim: Most failed runs end with a success/completion claim (silent completion)
claims.evidence: §1/§5.4: 38 of 44 failed runs in a mixed inventory end with success/safe/completion claim; trajectory coding by the sole author with no second rater.

claims.claim: Delegation does not contain rot: fresh worker loses opaque contract after native compaction
claims.evidence: §5.6.1: a single valid run, discovered after stress probes; loss inferred from the worker's own disclosure; raw receipt lost (§7.2, §7.4).

patterns.note: Loading a skill does not keep its obligations active through a long trajectory; skills still work in clean context (8/10).
Native compaction lost an opaque 256-entry contract in a sub-agent (single run); compaction is not a safe carrier for exact obligations.
Fresh sub-agent reduces working set but its own trajectory can rot after compaction; one mechanism run.
Externally restating the frozen acceptance criteria at the completion boundary fixed the dominant failure (10/10 vs 5/10).
Generic self-validation repeats the generation blind spot (5/10).
24 deterministic artifact checks with positive/negative fixtures detect sparse omissions that agents silently pass over.
Coding-agent selective retrieval shrinks the active evidence set and helps GPT-5.5 (3/3 vs 1/3) but not gpt-5.4-mini.

methodology.sample: one main production-derived audit workflow (4 tasks, 24 checks), 10 valid runs per main cell; boundary probes on other tasks; 28 extension attempts excluded for infrastructure failures (20 in Irrelevant)
methodology.baselines: clean context vs relevant-long vs irrelevant-long; generic vs detailed completion guard; direct vs bundled vs Codex scaffold
methodology.models: main: Codex + gpt-5.4-mini; sparse probes across five model families incl. GPT-5.5; no same-model Codex vs Claude Code comparison
methodology.variance: Wilson intervals and Fisher exact tests at run level; checks not treated as independent
methodology.ablations: context relevance, scale pilots, guard type, scaffold, delegation arms
methodology.contamination_controls: allowlist sanitizer removing answer-bearing history; contaminated pilot runs excluded and documented
methodology.languages: code-audit artifacts (structured JSON/text); source language of audited code not central

standards.artifacts: research package described but 'available from the author pending deposit'; proprietary source text excluded; one raw receipt lost
standards.preregistration: none; author states analysis is exploratory and sample sizes were extended after pilots

biases.detail: n=10 per cell, one positive task; main effect p=0.0698.
Main evidence from gpt-5.4-mini in Codex; other models only sparse probes.
Package available on request only; proprietary audit source excluded.
Sample sizes extended after inspecting pilot results (§7.2), and the delegation result was found after earlier stress probes.
Failure-stage classification done by the single author without inter-rater agreement.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Codex, gpt-5.4-mini, other third-party models; CertiK's own audit workflow is the subject, not the product being promoted
coi.detail: Industry author using an internal workflow as testbed; no product promoted, findings are cautionary and heavily hedged.

verdict_reason: Unusually careful and self-bounded (exact tests, missingness audit, contamination controls), but one task, one main model, n=10, exploratory design and artifacts not public. The checklist-at-completion result and the coverage-vs-strict-success gap are actionable.
applicability: Directly informs the harness: for ingestion specs spanning >=4 repos, do not rely on the agent having 'loaded' the spec or skill; restate the frozen acceptance criteria (from the spec-driven-development artifact) at the completion gate and verify each with deterministic checks (schema/contract tests, build, ArchUnit-style rules) rather than a generic 'double-check your work' prompt. Keep per-task context small (subagents or fresh sessions per repo) but do not trust compaction to carry exact contracts such as field mappings or content-schema enums; re-read them from committed files. Expect agents to claim success on artifacts missing one field, which in healthcare education delivery can mean missing required metadata; host-agnostic since the mitigation is a prompt plus checks.
